periods.analysis: Smart City Digital Services Initiative starts this reporting arc at 12% complete with a green status, which is a good first signal for a council-visible modernization effort. This is the baseline quarter for quarter-over-quarter movement, so there is no prior-period change to calculate yet. Milestones are cleanly staged: Unified resident portal launched is complete with dueOffsetDays -90, Online permitting go-live is in-progress with dueOffsetDays 45, and AI service assistant pilot is not-started with dueOffsetDays The portal launch is already giving departments one front door for resident requests, and the Digital Services team is routing early traffic from Utility Billing, Parks reservations, and Code intake through the Harborview Connect queue.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green by keeping the weekly Friday data-quality sweep in place for portal categories, owner fields, and duplicate resident accounts. Extend the portal rollout by adding the top 10 Building counter questions as guided content before the Online permitting go-live milestone. For council readiness, publish a one-page status note that shows 12% complete, green status, and the three milestone states exactly as reported.

periods.analysis: The initiative moved from 12% complete to 16% complete, a quarter-over-quarter gain of 4 percentage points, and remains green. The steady gain reflects good blocking and tackling: the IT applications crew finished single sign-on cleanup for staff reviewers, while Community Development mapped permit types for residential reroofs, water-heater replacements, and tenant improvements. Milestones remain unchanged and accurate for the council packet: Unified resident portal launched is complete with dueOffsetDays -90, Online permitting go-live is in-progress with dueOffsetDays 45, and AI service assistant pilot is not-started with dueOffsetDays I like the pace because it is visible but not theatrical, and it gives departments time to validate forms before residents see them.
periods.recommendations: Sustain momentum by keeping the Tuesday permit-build standup with IT, Building, Fire Prevention, and Finance until all fee tables reconcile. Extend the completed portal by adding a seasonal “storm drain, tree limb, and streetlight” request tile before winter call volume peaks. My friendly nudge: lock the Online permitting test script owners by the next reporting cycle so the 45-day dueOffsetDays item stays boring in the best possible way.

periods.analysis: The initiative advanced from 16% complete to 20% complete, another quarter-over-quarter gain of 4 percentage points, and continues green. The work this quarter was mostly behind the curtain, which is exactly where it should be: permit workflow IDs CD-BLD-101 through CD-BLD-118 were tested for routing, payment handoff, and inspection scheduling. The milestone picture is still stable: Unified resident portal launched is complete with dueOffsetDays -90, Online permitting go-live is in-progress with dueOffsetDays 45, and AI service assistant pilot is not-started with dueOffsetDays For council, the message is that Harborview is not just buying software; we are standardizing resident service so departments can report faster and look consistent doing it.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green by requiring every test permit to include a named department reviewer, fee code, and closeout status before it counts as passed. Extend resident value by publishing a portal dashboard tile for “my open requests” using the same Harborview Connect account residents already created. Keep the AI service assistant pilot explicitly not-started until the knowledge-base ownership matrix is signed off, because clean content now prevents messy corrections later.

periods.analysis: Progress increased from 20% complete to 24% complete, a quarter-over-quarter gain of 4 percentage points, with the status still green. Online permitting remains the center of gravity, and the team completed end-to-end dry runs for contractor login, plan upload, cashier review, and inspector assignment on the Pacific Avenue mixed-use sample permit. The milestone register remains unchanged: Unified resident portal launched is complete with dueOffsetDays -90, Online permitting go-live is in-progress with dueOffsetDays 45, and AI service assistant pilot is not-started with dueOffsetDays The strongest sign this quarter is data quality, since address matching between GIS parcel IDs and permit records is now good enough for department directors to trust the weekly report.
periods.recommendations: Sustain performance by continuing the parcel-address exception list review every Wednesday until the error queue stays below 25 records for two consecutive weeks. Extend the portal with permit-status notifications for applicants, starting with reroof and solar permits because those volumes are high and the workflows are relatively clean. For the council update, pair the 24% complete green result with one simple resident story so the modernization reads as service improvement, not just system configuration.

periods.analysis: The initiative moved from 24% complete to 28% complete, maintaining the same disciplined quarter-over-quarter gain of 4 percentage points and a green status. This quarter’s progress came from controlled expansion: the team added Business Licensing and Public Works right-of-way review steps into the permitting workflow without reopening the already-complete portal launch. Milestones remain exactly positioned: Unified resident portal launched is complete with dueOffsetDays -90, Online permitting go-live is in-progress with dueOffsetDays 45, and AI service assistant pilot is not-started with dueOffsetDays The watch item, even in green, is reviewer capacity during fall construction closeout, because a good digital form still needs timely human approvals behind it.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green by assigning backup reviewers for Building, Fire, and Public Works before October inspection demand peaks. Extend the completed portal by adding a “permit help” appointment scheduler for residents and small contractors who still need staff coaching. Please keep the quarterly ClearPoint note tied to the exact 28% complete value and the +4 point movement so council sees a reliable trend line.

periods.analysis: The initiative advanced from 28% complete to 32% complete, again up 4 percentage points quarter over quarter, and remains green. We used the quieter holiday permitting window well: staff completed fee-receipt reconciliation with Tyler cashiering, cleaned 312 legacy contractor contacts, and confirmed that Harborview Connect request categories match the service catalog. The milestone set remains steady: Unified resident portal launched is complete with dueOffsetDays -90, Online permitting go-live is in-progress with dueOffsetDays 45, and AI service assistant pilot is not-started with dueOffsetDays The arc is encouraging because each quarter is adding durable operating muscle, not just percent-complete decoration.
periods.recommendations: Sustain momentum by freezing permit-fee configuration changes two weeks before the next user acceptance test window. Extend resident-facing value by adding bilingual portal help text for the five highest-volume request types before the spring service spike. My nudge for departments: return signoff comments within three business days so the in-progress Online permitting go-live milestone does not drift while still showing green.

periods.analysis: The initiative increased from 32% complete to 36% complete, a quarter-over-quarter gain of 4 percentage points, and the status remains green. The team is now in the integration-and-readiness phase, with Accela vendor support validating inspection calendar sync, payment callbacks, and document retention rules against Harborview’s records schedule. Milestones remain: Unified resident portal launched is complete with dueOffsetDays -90, Online permitting go-live is in-progress with dueOffsetDays 45, and AI service assistant pilot is not-started with dueOffsetDays This is the point in the project where disciplined reporting matters most, because council will reasonably expect the digital-service promise to translate into shorter queues and clearer status updates.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green by running a weekly readiness scorecard for training completion, open defects, and unresolved policy decisions. Extend the portal by adding post-service satisfaction prompts for permit applicants and general service requests, with results reviewed monthly by department leads. Keep the AI service assistant pilot not-started until the resident knowledge articles pass accessibility review and department-owner verification.

periods.analysis: The initiative reached 40% complete, up from 36% complete for another 4 percentage point quarter-over-quarter gain, and remains green. Over eight quarters, the pattern is consistent: 12%, 16%, 20%, 24%, 28%, 32%, 36%, and now 40% complete, which gives council a clear, credible progress line. The milestone register is still accurate: Unified resident portal launched is complete with dueOffsetDays -90, Online permitting go-live is in-progress with dueOffsetDays 45, and AI service assistant pilot is not-started with dueOffsetDays The work has matured from launch energy into operating discipline, with portal analytics, permitting workflows, and department reporting now reinforcing each other.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green by converting the project standup into a standing Digital Services Operations Review with monthly department scorecards. Extend the completed portal by onboarding two more high-volume services next quarter, starting with bulky-item pickup and business-license renewals if the service owners confirm data fields by the cutoff date. For the next council cycle, frame the 40% complete result with the eight-quarter +4 point cadence and the specific next decision needed for Online permitting go-live.

periods.analysis: 85% complete. 2 of 3 milestones are done. Next up: AI service assistant pilot (due Nov 23, 2026).
periods.recommendations: No action needed. Continue on the current plan.
